artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan landing both recommended fixes: a --check/--write provides.scripts repair script, and a narrow self-attribution screen on the baseline-tolerant pre-existing-findings branch at both completion call sites, with behavioral fixtures and docs.

memory_candidates.content: A pre/post deploy comparison cannot gate a check whose SUBJECT lives in the source store. The orchestrate redeploy checkpoint and command-gate-out.sh's rc==6 handler both decide 'did this redeploy introduce a new finding?' by set-differencing verify-deploy.sh --findings snapshots taken immediately before and after deploy-headless.sh. Only the deploy tree changes between those two calls, so any check that reads committed source-store state (check-extension-docs.sh resolves EXT_DIR to agent-system/extensions/ even when invoked via its deployed copy -- Rules Q/H/A and any future disk-driven rule) yields an IDENTICAL verdict in both snapshots. Its violation is therefore always classified 'temporally pre-existing' and waved through, even when the very task about to be marked COMPLETED is what committed it. Temporal pre-existence and causal attribution are indistinguishable in that measurement window. The general lesson: a differential gate only detects defects whose subject changes inside the differential's own window; for anything outside it, add a positive self-attribution test against the completing unit's own modified_files rather than widening the window. The fail-safe polarity inverts between the two uses -- an attribution filter that CLEARS a finding must fail safe toward blocking, while a narrowing filter added to an already-proceeding branch must fail safe toward proceeding, or it bricks every completion whenever any identifier-free red finding exists.
